research_concepts: teammate DRIVE immediately preceding a PNR possession
pick-and-roll possession points per possession (PNR PPP)
play-type labeling from play-by-play action types
sequential play-type effects within an offense
derived play-type possession records from the graph database
methodological_questions: Does a teammate DRIVE in the preceding possession raise PNR PPP relative to other preceding play types, after conditioning on game state and lineup?
Are PNR and DRIVE labels valid enough, and is the preceding-possession link reliable enough, to support a sequential contrast?
What placebo, reversed-order and label-validation checks are needed to separate a sequencing effect from labeling artifacts and selection?
What sample size is needed for a sequential contrast, given that DRIVE-to-PNR transitions are a subset of PNR possessions?

historical_evidence.finding: Play-type label backfill verification on 921,514 possessions. PNR share 28.7% (FAIL against band 20-28%), PULL_UP 7.9% FAIL, 3100 games with team PNR >33% FAIL. PNR PPP 0.948 PASS, temporal PASS, team identity FAIL. 82.8% of PNR labels are proxy_calibrated. Final verdict recorded as FAIL.

Play-type label accuracy audit. Overall FAIL: OTHER 20.2% against a <10% target, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark, most play types have PPP above benchmark band, MIA identity checks fail. Verdict recorded as tool_eval_fail.

Labeling audit of OTHER/DRIVE foul leakage. 36% of OTHER possessions end in fouls, inflating OTHER PPP. DRIVE sits 12pp below the foul benchmark. PNR shows a 22% foul rate. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) map to a real play type via initiation_type. Verdict recorded as artifact_found.
On-ball defensive scheme labels for ORL-DET G1. Only 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of on-ball half-court possessions are labeled. switches_on not populated. Verdict recorded as failed_gate.

A1 adaptation falsification tests. Adapter dPPP +0.0667 (n=205), no_signal +0.1260 (n=57), wrong_way +0.0111 (n=274). Next-game PPP Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842. Recorded as a C_artifact failure with LABEL_ERROR and MECHANICAL_FLOOR risks.
Play-type PPP across playoff series game buckets (1197 records, no CIs). PNR +0.087 across buckets. Recorded as observational with selection caveats, with the verdict 'NO CLEAR SIGNAL'.
PNR shot-level season rates across 30 teams (2024-25). Rates range from OKC 7.567% to IND 13.824%. Calibrated PNR is about 17.9-19.6% of possessions. No validation recorded.

Net-swing play-type prototype on 104 team-offense units. Top recommendation changes in 38% of units. DRIVE median net swing -0.27 (negative in 88%). Not evaluated against outcomes. Verdict recorded as descriptive.

52-series sequential adaptation test. durable_branches is empty. Pivot branches were not durable. DRIVE/POST_UP negative net swing recorded as the durable finding. Mechanism recorded as B_powered_null.

Superstar suppression by lineup and forced play type (Jokic, Curry, Doncic, Giannis). Lineup PPP gaps reported, with no placebo or matching. Later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using OTHER/DRIVE/PNR PPP differences as real efficiency evidence, with play types from initiation_type
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact. Foul endings inflate OTHER PPP, DRIVE is under-labeled by foul benchmark, and initiation_type maps only 0.7% of possessions to a real play type.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferred play-type labels as a valid basis for adaptation findings
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact and tool_eval_fail. OTHER is 20.2% against a <10% target, foul possessions leak into OTHER, and DRIVE foul-draw is 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Backfilled PNR and PULL_UP labels against expected league distributions
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as FAIL. PNR share and PULL_UP share fail band checks, 82.8% of PNR labels are proxy_calibrated, and team identity fails.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing an A1 adapter PPP lift to real coverage response
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as C_artifact. The wrong-way and no-signal contrasts do not behave as predicted, and next-game carryover is null (p=0.842).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labeling on-ball defensive schemes from matchup fields
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as failed_gate with untestable status. Label rates are 14.9% and 3.3%, and switches_on is not populated.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Star-initiator lineup and forced-play-type suppression contrasts
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching was used. The record notes later work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type PPP change across playoff series as an adaptation signal
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as inconclusive with no CIs and selection caveats. The DRIVE signal is stable or improving across series, not declining.

evidence_establishes: Play-type labels in this project's derived records have repeatedly failed validation gates (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF-CHT-025). PNR and DRIVE labels are part of those failures.
Most PNR labels in the backfilled data are proxy_calibrated (82.8%, FAM:SF-APPA-030). The PNR label is therefore partly constructed rather than observed.
No retrieved record tests whether a teammate DRIVE immediately preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP. The sequential contrast has not been answered in this project's retrieved history.
Earlier sequential or adaptation tests in this project (FAM:SF-APPS-049, FAM:SF-APPA-001, FAM:SF-APPS-010) were null, inconclusive or artifact, and none isolated the DRIVE-to-PNR transition.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the DRIVE-to-PNR effect exists in the true game process. No record reports an estimate for this specific contrast.
Whether the 2022-23 to 2025-26 play-by-play supports a valid DRIVE-to-PNR link. Preceding-possession linkage was not validated in any retrieved record.
Any effect size, confidence interval or power calculation for DRIVE-to-PNR PPP.
Whether the 2025-26 partial data changes results, since that season's regular-season and playoff completeness depends on the retrieval date.
own_inferences: The question is not answerable with confidence until the label validation failures are resolved. The preceding-possession link depends on the same DRIVE and PNR labels that failed audit.
PNR PPP partly depends on outcome-derived labels (points-based calibration). Any test of PNR PPP as an outcome is at risk of OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL circularity.
Teammate DRIVE sequences are likely correlated with game state (fast-break, trailing, clock), so a raw contrast is confounded by possession context and team quality.
A consistent, validated sequential design would need a reference set of preceding play types (SPOT_UP, HANDOFF, ISO) to serve as comparators and as a placebo.
uncertainties: Whether initiation_type or the graph possession records can reliably link the immediately preceding teammate possession to the PNR possession, given the 0.7% mapping rate (FAM:SF-CHT-025).
The fraction of DRIVE and PNR possessions that are observed rather than proxy-calibrated.
Whether 2025-26 partial-season data is complete enough for any test (regular season complete from 2026-04-13; playoffs complete from 2026-06-21, so the playoff window is still open on 2026-06-14).
Power: no record reports DRIVE-to-PNR sample sizes. The number of DRIVE-preceded PNR possessions is unknown.
Whether any unretrieved records exist. Only the retrieved records were available; no follow-up tools were called.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the retrieved history, a direct test using the play-by-play labels as they stand might have proceeded. The audit records (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF-CHT-025) show that PNR and DRIVE labels and their sequencing have failed validation in this project. The decision therefore moves from proceed to do_not_proceed until the label gate is passed. Earlier null and artifact findings in sequential adaptation (FAM:SF-APPS-049, FAM:SF-APPA-001) also argue against a raw sequential estimate.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR and DRIVE labels failed audit gates (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF-CHT-025). 82.8% of PNR labels are proxy-calibrated and 0.7% of possessions map via initiation_type.
PNR calibration uses points-based PPP targets, so PNR PPP as an outcome partly reflects the labeling process.
The preceding-possession link and the PNR label may be assigned using information from the outcome possession.
DRIVE sequences are associated with game state, personnel and team quality, which are not controlled in any retrieved record.
DRIVE-preceded PNR possessions are a subset of PNR possessions, and their count per team and season is unknown.
No placebo or reversed-order check has been run in this project's sequential work (FAM:SF-CHT-009 notes no placebo).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests whether a teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP. Related work covers PNR and DRIVE PPP across series (SF-APPS-010, inconclusive), a sequential adaptation test that found no durable branch (SF-APPS-049, rejected), and label audits that failed or found artifacts (SF-APPA-030, SF-APPM-014, SF-CHT-025). These are related but do not answer the sequential question.

risks.text: Play-type labels failed multiple audit gates (SF-APPA-030, SF-APPM-014, SF-CHT-025). A test on these labels would mostly measure labeling error.
PNR labels are calibrated against points outcomes, so PNR PPP is partly constructed from its own outcome.
The preceding-possession link and label assignment could use information from the outcome possession, inflating the contrast.
Game state, clock, score margin, personnel, opponent defense and team quality may drive both DRIVE sequences and PNR efficiency.
Possessions are selected by prior events (a DRIVE is more likely after a stop or a rebound), which can produce regression-to-the-mean in PNR PPP.
The DRIVE-to-PNR subset is unlikely to be large enough for a stable contrast within team and season; no power calculation exists.
Teammate DRIVE followed by PNR may be rare, especially for low-usage lineups, leaving many cells empty.
Many play-type pairings and buckets were examined across earlier families; a single post-hoc contrast from this set would be vulnerable to selection.
Without placebo sequences (e.g., SPOT_UP before PNR), a positive DRIVE effect cannot be distinguished from generic sequence or star effects (SF-CHT-009).
Pooling 2022-23 to 2025-26 mixes rule and style changes, and 2025-26 is partial before its completion dates.
PPP for short or low-count cells can sit at a mechanical floor or ceiling, distorting the contrast (SF-APPA-001 risk).

design.estimand: Within-offense difference in PNR PPP when the immediately preceding possession is a teammate DRIVE versus the same contrast when it is a non-DRIVE play type, conditional on game state, lineup and opponent. Proceed only after the label gate is passed.
design.unit: PNR possession, linked to the immediately preceding offensive possession by the same team.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23 to 2024-25 for discovery, after label validation. 2025-26 regular season (complete) as confirmatory holdout. Playoffs excluded from primary analysis. 2025-26 playoffs only after completion (from 2026-06-21).
design.power: Not computed. Must be set before analysis using the observed DRIVE-preceded PNR count after the label gate. Target a minimum detectable effect and stop if the DRIVE-preceded subset is below a pre-registered count.
design.controls: Team and season fixed effects, score margin band, clock and period, possession count, opponent defensive rating, lineup or personnel, and defensive matchup minutes where available. Exclude the outcome possession from any preceding-link assignment to avoid leakage. Use a pre-registered label-validation pass (PNR share in band, foul leakage rate, initiation_type mapping rate) as a precondition.
design.falsification: (a) Placebo sequences: SPOT_UP, HANDOFF and ISO preceding PNR should show no comparable lift. (b) Reversed order: PNR preceding DRIVE should not show the same effect. (c) Negative control: DRIVE preceding non-PNR outcomes. A DRIVE effect that also appears in placebo sequences is an artifact.
design.multiplicity: One primary contrast (DRIVE-preceded vs non-DRIVE-preceded PNR PPP). Placebo and reversed-order contrasts are secondary and reported with correction (e.g., Holm).
design.decision_rule: Support only if the primary contrast's 95% CI excludes zero, the effect is absent in all placebo and reversed-order contrasts, it replicates in the 2025-26 regular-season holdout, and the label-validation gate passes. Otherwise report as uncertain or artifact.
design.data_version: NBA stats API play-by-play for 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons (frozen before analysis), and 2025-26 regular season after 2026-04-13. Derived graph possession records and labels versioned and frozen with the audit outputs. Playoffs excluded until 2025-26 completion.

methodological_questions: Does a teammate drive before a pick-and-roll raise pick-and-roll points per possession?
Are play-type labels derived from outcomes or from raw action types, and how reliable are they?
What sample size, exposure and confounding controls are needed for sequential play-type effects?
args.query: effect of teammate DRIVE preceding PNR on PNR points per possession; play-type labeling reliability and data quality in NBA play-by-play 2022-23 to 2025-26

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
